free_tier.stated: All researchers from any discipline, both inside and out of the Harvard University community, can deposit files of up to 2.5GB, and store up to 1TB of data on the Harvard Dataverse Repository.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: All researchers from any discipline, both inside and out of the Harvard University community, can deposit files of up to 2.5GB, and store up to 1TB of data on the Harvard Dataverse Repository.
per_object_cap.notes: The 2.5 GB limit is stated for a file deposited; the same sentence gives 1 TB as the data a researcher can store.

retention.stated: Once a dataset is published it cannot be unpublished and can only be deaccessioned under extreme circumstances, such as a legal requirement to destroy that dataset.
retention.notes: Harvard states it supports permanent bit-level preservation of all materials directly deposited in the Harvard Dataverse.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Public file access returns 303 -> a presigned S3 URL (dvn-cloud-iqss.s3.amazonaws.com) valid 3600s; S3 honours Range requests. No egress pricing exists anywhere in the product. Probe: GET /api/access/datafile/11685194 -L -H 'Range: bytes=0-1023' -> 303 then HTTP 206, Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/21269528, Server: AmazonS3.

tooling: Native REST API v6.10.1 (live: GET /api/info/version -> {"version":"6.10.1"}); SWORD v2 deposit; OAI-PMH harvest; S3 direct-upload API for files >2.5 GB (docs: 'This option can handle files >300GB'). Python client pyDataverse; R package dataverse. No rclone backend, but a REST loop is trivial (~15 lines) and the platform is a well-documented Invenio-free Java stack.
chaining: Collection creation is open to any logged-in user. The quota endpoint returns a 1 TiB allocation (1,099,511,627,776 bytes) for some collections and no quota for others, so a per-collection allocation is not shown for every collection.

limits_note: Per-file 2.5 GB through the Harvard UI/API; larger files require the S3 direct-upload path, which Harvard has enabled (downloads already redirect to S3, so upload-redirect is configured). Dataset file-count cap observed live: effectiveDatasetFileCountLimit=1000 (12 used on the sampled dataset). No enforced collection quota: GET /api/dataverses/harvard/storage/quota?showInherited=true -> {"message":"No quota defined for this collection"}. Publishing is a 'Submit for Review' spam-check gate, not peer review.

extras.agent_focus: Open-science repositories with per-project/per-file quotas (excluding Zenodo, owned by another agent). Central question: is 20 TiB of non-research data technically placeable, and does private/unpublished staging count against quota (i.e. is the repo usable as working storage, not just as a publish target).

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
